IDEO Foundations

Design Principles that guide Meld

Five core tenets shaping every token, component, and interaction model in the system.

01 · Cohesion

Consistency

Create predictable, intuitive experiences across products and platforms. Shared token semantics guarantee cohesive behavior everywhere.

02 · Inclusion

Accessibility

Make experiences usable by people with diverse abilities. WCAG 2.2 AA contrast, 40px touch minimums, and keyboard accessibility by default.

03 · Purpose

Clarity

Prioritise understandable interfaces and meaningful interactions. Remove visual clutter and make interactive states unambiguous.

04 · Scale

Flexibility

Support varying product domains from consumer apps to high-density enterprise data grids without compromising design integrity.

05 · Future

Scalability

Build enduring architectural foundations that evolve seamlessly with teams, products, and new technology paradigms.

Section 01 — Overview

Typography

IDEO Website Design System

This module establishes the rules for typeface selection, hierarchy, sizing, spacing, responsive behavior, and implementation. It is a proposed specification, not an official IDEO brand guideline.

TypefaceSpace GroteskVersion1.0
StatusProposed specificationScopeWebsite-wide typography
Primary goalEstablish a consistent and reusable typography language.

Ideas into impact.

Typography creates clarity, establishes hierarchy, and gives every digital experience a consistent voice.

Five system layers

    Section 02 — Typeface Foundations

    Space Grotesk

    Primary typeface for the entire website. Use 400, 500 and 600 for most interface typography; reserve 700 for selected emphasis.

    ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ
    abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
    0123456789
    !@#$%&*()_+-=[]{}

    Weights

    Specification

    Primary family tokenfont.family.primary → "Space Grotesk"
    Fallback familyfont.family.fallback → Arial, sans-serif
    Supported weights300–700 via the Google Fonts variable file (wght@300..700). Light (300) is a foundation weight only; it has no primitive token.
    Font-loading behaviordisplay=swap: fallback text renders immediately, then swaps once Space Grotesk loads. Content stays readable if loading fails.

    Primitive tokens

    Raw values. Rem conversions assume a 16px root. Copy buttons copy the CSS declaration.

    D. Letter spacing

    Semantic styles

    Desktop reference values. A visual “H1” style is not necessarily an <h1> element: choose the HTML element for document hierarchy, then apply the style.

    Color module · 01 — Overview
    Color System
    

    IDEO Website Design System
    

    Version 1.0 · Status: Proposed system specification. The color system establishes brand identity, hierarchy, usability, interaction states, accessibility and theme consistency. Only the two brand colors are approved inputs; every other value is proposed and pending design approval, not official IDEO guidance.
    

    

    Token flow

    Color module · 02 — Brand Color Palette
    Brand palette
    

    Approved values, preserved exactly. All contrast ratios are calculated live with the WCAG relative-luminance formula.
    

    Brand combinations
    

    

    

    Color module · 03 — Primitive Color Tokens
    Primitive tokens
    

    Raw values independent of purpose. Neutrals and feedback colors are proposed. Pink and indigo scales are derived in OKLCH (constant lightness steps, gamut-clamped to sRGB) and are supporting palettes, not replacements for the brand tokens. Feedback colors stay visually distinct from the brand hues and are pending validation. “W” and “K” show contrast against white and #171717.
    

    

    

    

    Color module · 04 — Semantic Color Tokens
    Semantic tokens
    

    Purpose-based aliases that reference primitives (proposed mappings). Each shows its light and dark resolution.
    

    

    

    

    Color module · 05 — Light and Dark Themes
    Themes
    

    The same semantic tokens resolve to different primitives per theme. Dark is not an inversion: surfaces and tones are balanced separately and the brand tokens are never altered. The switcher also sits in the header.
    

    

    

    

    Color module · 06 — Application Guide
    Application guide
    

    Live examples built only from component tokens. Buttons, links, cards, forms and feedback are shown in light and dark side by side.
    

    

    

    Color module · 07 — Component Color Tokens
    Component tokens
    

    Component tokens reference semantic tokens only. The two swatches show the resolved light and dark values.
    

    

    

    Color module · 08 — Accessibility and Contrast Checker
    Contrast checker
    

    Thresholds (WCAG 2.2 AA): normal text 4.5:1; large text (18pt regular / 14pt bold) 3:1; meaningful UI components and graphics 3:1. Passing one does not imply passing the others. This tool validates chosen pairs only; it does not certify the website as WCAG compliant. Brand hex values are never changed automatically.
    

    

    

    

    

    Required test combinations (calculated)
    

    • Color must not be the only means of communicating information.
    • Focus indicators must stay visible against every background.
    • Disabled elements should remain understandable (labels, not just faded color).
    • Links need sufficient contrast and a non-color cue such as an underline.
    • Brand identity does not override accessibility requirements.

    Color module · 10 — Token Architecture
    Primitive → semantic → component
    

    Semantic and component tokens reference other tokens and never duplicate raw HEX values. Light and dark modes resolve the same semantic token to different primitives.
    

    

    Primitive
    • color.brand.primary
    • color.brand.secondary
    • color.neutral.950
    • color.neutral.50
    →
    

    Semantic
    • color.text.primary
    • color.surface.page
    • color.action.primary
    →
    

    Component
    • button.primary.background
    • card.background
    • input.border
    

    Theme mapping: color.text.primary → color.neutral.950 in light, color.neutral.50 in dark. Components are unchanged.
    

    

    

    Color module · 11 — Figma Implementation Guide
    Figma variables
    

    1. Collection “Primitives” (one mode): groups brand, neutral, pink, indigo, success, warning, error, information. Create color variables such as brand/primary = #BC4989 and neutral/950 = #171717 using the values in Section 03.
      2. 

    2. Collection “Semantic” with modes Light and Dark: groups text, surface, action, border, icon. Every variable is an alias to a primitive, e.g. text/primary → Light: neutral/950, Dark: neutral/50 (see Section 04).
      3. 

    3. Collection “Components”: groups button, card, input, navigation, link, each aliasing a semantic variable (Section 07).
      4. 

    4. Apply Components or Semantic variables to fills and strokes of reusable components, then switch the frame’s variable mode to test Light and Dark.
    

    Figma variable collections are design-file constructs; CSS custom properties (Section 12) are the code equivalent. Creating variables does not by itself restyle existing components or configure the codebase: each fill and stroke must be bound to a variable.

    Color module · 13 — Usage Guidelines
    Usage guidelines
    

    Do
    • Preserve approved brand colors.
    • Use semantic tokens in components.
    • Balance expressive brand accents with neutrals.
    • Validate contrast for actual pairs.
    • Keep semantic meaning the same across themes.
    • Use feedback colors consistently.
    • Use color to establish hierarchy.
    • Test states against the real component background.
    

    Don’t
    • Hard-code random HEX values in components.
    • Use brand colors for every background.
    • Assume white text works on every light tint.
    • Use color alone for errors or success.
    • Change a brand color for one component without documenting it.
    • Reuse a raw color for unrelated purposes without an intentional alias.
    • Claim compliance without testing real components.

    Components module · 01 — Overview
    Components
    

    Proposed component specification for Meld by IDEO: 13 categories and the full requested inventory, each with priority metadata, anatomy, variants, sizes, states, properties, behavior, accessibility, token mapping, Figma recreation guidance and an acceptance checklist. Colors and typography come from the modules above; anything not defined there is marked Proposed.
    

    Honesty note. Specs are written at archetype level (for example “button-like action” or “date picker”) and then personalised per component with its name, category, priority and neighbours. Treat component-specific details as review items. Previews are simulations in this page: nothing is uploaded, paid for, authenticated or sent to a backend.
    

    

    Categories and priority
    

    P0 Core · P1 Extended · P2 Specialised (conditional, build when a real use case exists). Priority never removes a component from the inventory.
    

    Shared state model
    

    States used: Default/Rest, Hover, Focus-visible, Pressed/Active, Selected, Disabled, Loading, Invalid/Error, Success, Read-only, Empty, Expanded/Collapsed, Checked/Unchecked/Indeterminate, Dragging/Drag-over, Visited, responsive behavior, Light and Dark. Each component documents only the meaningful subset.
    

    DistinctionRule
    

    Disabled vs read-onlyDisabled is not focusable or editable and is excluded from submission. Read-only stays focusable and readable, and is submitted but not editable.
    

    Selected vs pressedSelected is a persistent choice (tab, option). Pressed is the momentary active moment, or a toggle’s on state, exposed with aria-pressed.
    

    Invalid vs error feedbackInvalid is the field state (aria-invalid plus border). Error feedback is the message that explains and fixes it. Both are needed.
    

    Loading vs disabledLoading is temporary and busy (aria-busy) while content or context stays visible. Disabled is unavailable until something changes.
    

    Component vs application stateComponents own visual and interaction states. Application states (offline, quota reached, no permission) are passed in as props and shown with Feedback components.
    

    Valid combinationsExamples: loading button (non-interactive), invalid field that is also focused, checked and disabled checkbox, selected tab with keyboard focus, table loading while rows stay visible. Impossible combinations (loading + hover feedback) are not documented.

        What the Library Contains
      
      
      
      
        The visual source of truth for all primitive tokens, UI components, and layouts:

        How Designers Use the Library
      
      
      
      
        Guidelines for integrating Meld into project files and team workflows:
      
      
      
        
        
      • Instance Composition: Always insert component instances from the assets panel. Never detach master components.
        • 
        
      • Variable Mode Binding: Bind screen frames to the Meld variable collection to automatically inherit dark mode contrast.
        • 
        
      • Responsive Constraints: Use Auto Layout (Fill container / Hug contents) to mirror engineering flexbox rules.
        •

      Figma Component Handoff Conventions
      
    
        
      
      1. Naming Standard: Use slash syntax: Meld / [Category] / [Component] (e.g. Meld / Forms / Text Field). Variant properties read Variant = Primary, Size = Medium, State = Default.
        2. 
      
      2. Component Sets: Use component sets when components have two or more variant dimensions. Compose larger parts from nested instances, never detached frames.
        3. 
      
      3. Boolean Properties: Optional parts use Boolean properties (Leading Icon), labels use Text properties, and replaceable icons use Instance-swap.
        4. 
      
      4. Auto Layout: Every component uses Auto Layout with explicit padding and gap tokens matching system spacing.
        5. 
      
      5. Variables: Bind fills, strokes, and text to the Semantic color collection and typography styles.
        6. 
      
      6. States: Model Default, Hover, Focus-visible, Pressed, and Disabled as the State variant property.
        7. 
      
      7. Accessibility Verification: Creating components in Figma does not enforce accessibility; keyboard behavior, focus management, and screen-reader announcements are engineering verification items.
        8.

      Patterns module · 01 - Overview
      UX Patterns
      
  
      Patterns are reusable, structured solutions to recurring user experience challenges across IDEO digital products. Where components represent atomic UI building blocks (buttons, inputs, cards), patterns orchestrate multiple components, interaction sequences, system feedback, and behavioral rules into coherent, accessible workflows.
      
  
  
      
    
      
      
        
      ScopeIDEO digital experiences, enterprise applications, design tools, and AI workflows
      
        
      Categories8 Core Categories • 125 Fully Documented UX Patterns
      
        
      AI IntegrationWorkflows A (Content Generation), B (Human Approval), and C (Agentic Workflows)
      
        
      ComplianceWCAG 2.2 AA Accessibility, Dual-Theme (Light & Dark), Responsive reflow
      
            
    
      
  
      

  
      Pattern Maturity & Classification
      
  
      
    
      
      
      P0 — Core
      
      Essential & Foundational
      
      Universal requirements for any product: Sign In/Up, Form validation, Search & Data tables, Feedback modals, Global navigation, File intake.
      
    
      
    
      
      
      P1 — Standard
      
      Common Product Workflows
      
      Standard patterns required across multiple products: Onboarding tours, Bulk actions, Master-detail views, Inline editing, Conversational AI interfaces.
      
    
      
    
      
      
      P2 — Specialized
      
      Domain-Specific & Advanced
      
      Advanced patterns: Multi-Factor Authentication, Agent permission requests, Human approval workflows, Live progress tracking.
      
    
      
    
      
      
      P3 — Exploratory
      
      Emerging & Agentic
      
      Next-generation interactions: Multi-step autonomous agent execution, memory/context controls, collaborative multi-agent handoffs.

        Patterns module · 03 - Figma Recreation Guide
        Recreating UX patterns in Figma
        
  
        Patterns are not oversized monolithic master components. In Figma, patterns are system assemblies composed of existing Meld components, structured with Auto Layout and variable modes.
        
  
  
          
    
        1. Assembly over Monoliths: Assemble patterns from instances of canonical Meld components (Button, Text Field, Modal, Card, Badge). Do not detach components.
          2. 
    
        2. Figma Page Organization: Group patterns in Figma under Patterns / [Category] / [Pattern Name] (e.g. Patterns / AI / Human-in-the-Loop Approval).
          3. 
    
        3. Responsive Frame Sets: Document each pattern across three responsive breakpoints: Desktop (1280px / 1440px), Tablet (768px), and Mobile (375px / 390px) using Auto Layout with fill-container rules.
          4. 
    
        4. Dual Variable Modes: Bind every fill, stroke, and typography style to the Meld token collections. Toggle between Light and Dark mode on the parent frame to verify high contrast across all states.
          5. 
    
        5. Interactive Prototype Flows: Use Figma component interactions for state transitions (Hover, Pressed, Focused, Open/Closed) and create linked prototype flows for multi-step sequences (e.g. Onboarding Stepper, Human Approval Gate, AI Token Streaming).
          6. 
    
        6. Engineering Handoff Annotations: Explicitly annotate asynchronous behaviors that cannot be fully expressed in Figma prototypes: screen reader live region announcements (aria-live), focus restoration, API timeouts, and fallback error recovery.
          7.
